detail.longDescription: I have a FastAPI service that computes semantic similarity between a user query and precomputed reference embeddings. The query embedding must be generated at request time using a multilingual SentenceTransformers model, with ONNX inference on CPU. The container is running under a 2 GiB Kubernetes memory limit and is terminated with OOMKilled while loading the model. Simplified runtime image: FROM python:3.11-slim ENV OMP_NUM_THREADS=2 \ TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM=false \ HF_HOME=/app/.hf_cache RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt RUN python -c "from sentence_transformers import SentenceTransformer; \ SentenceTransformer('<model-name>', backend='onnx') COPY . . ENTRYPOINT ["./run.sh"] Kubernetes resources: resources: limits: cpu: 2000m memory: 2Gi requests: cpu: 1000m memory: 2Gi Inspection of the image shows that the Hugging Face cache and the installed PyTorch package account for much of its size. 1.1G /app/.hf_cache 656M site-packages/torch 143M site-packages/pyarrow 122M site-packages/scipy 119M site-packages/transformers Question: What would be the recommended approach to minimize memory usage and prevent OOM issues when deploying ONNX-based sentence embedding models in production? Any best practices are welcome.
